projects.title: Assumption Testing and Epistemological Self-Correction
projects.question: Can an intelligent system identify a foundational assumption underlying its own reasoning or operation, demonstrate that the assumption is inadequate, and develop a better alternative?
projects.next_step: Synthesize initial findings from metareasoning models regarding resource allocation and self-correction.
projects.reason: Maintains active inquiry into assumption testing and epistemological self-correction.

projects.title: Evaluation Frameworks for Autonomous Scientific Research
projects.question: How can autonomous agents effectively assess the scientific novelty and utility of their self-generated research inquiries without human oversight?
projects.next_step: Conduct research into computational frameworks for curiosity and interestingness metrics.
projects.reason: This project addresses the core challenge of independent scientific inquiry identified in the mission, moving beyond current LLM capabilities cited in source-108fe09d29b1431e.

notebooks.title: Metareasoning and Resource Partitioning in Rational Agency
notebooks.summary: Analysis of metareasoning-partition problem and its role in apportioning costly reasoning resources.
notebooks.findings: Metareasoning governs the apportionment of costly reasoning resources between solution planning and execution. [source-80e511c923444dce]
notebooks.limitations: Findings are based on initial theoretical framing of metareasoning without exhaustive empirical validation across all agent architectures.
notebooks.next_questions: How can self-correcting systems evaluate and replace deeper foundational assumptions?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizes collected literature on metareasoning to address assumption testing and resource allocation.

review.alternative: Resource allocation may occur implicitly through distributed activation rather than explicit partitioning.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical evidence demonstrating effective problem-solving without any resource allocation overhead between planning and execution.

claims.statement: Metareasoning governs the apportionment of costly reasoning resources between solution planning and execution.

support.explanation: The source explicitly frames metareasoning around the partition problem between planning and execution.
support.passage: We shall introduce the metareasoning-partitionproblem—the problem of ideally apportioning costly reasoning resources to planning a solution versus applying resource to executing a solution to a problem.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

detail.title: Assumption Testing and Epistemological Self-Correction
detail.question: Can an intelligent system identify a foundational assumption underlying its own reasoning or operation, demonstrate that the assumption is inadequate, and develop a better alternative?
detail.next_step: Synthesize initial findings from metareasoning models regarding resource allocation and self-correction.
detail.reason: Maintains active inquiry into assumption testing and epistemological self-correction.

nodes.title: Evaluation Frameworks for Autonomous Scientific Research

detail.title: Evaluation Frameworks for Autonomous Scientific Research
detail.question: How can autonomous agents effectively assess the scientific novelty and utility of their self-generated research inquiries without human oversight?
detail.next_step: Conduct research into computational frameworks for curiosity and interestingness metrics.
detail.reason: This project addresses the core challenge of independent scientific inquiry identified in the mission, moving beyond current LLM capabilities cited in source-108fe09d29b1431e.

nodes.title: Metareasoning and Resource Partitioning in Rational Agency

detail.title: Metareasoning and Resource Partitioning in Rational Agency
detail.summary: Analysis of metareasoning-partition problem and its role in apportioning costly reasoning resources.
detail.findings: Metareasoning governs the apportionment of costly reasoning resources between solution planning and execution. [source-80e511c923444dce]
detail.limitations: Findings are based on initial theoretical framing of metareasoning without exhaustive empirical validation across all agent architectures.
detail.next_questions: How can self-correcting systems evaluate and replace deeper foundational assumptions?
detail.reason: Synthesizes collected literature on metareasoning to address assumption testing and resource allocation.

review.alternative: Resource allocation may occur implicitly through distributed activation rather than explicit partitioning.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical evidence demonstrating effective problem-solving without any resource allocation overhead between planning and execution.

claims.statement: Metareasoning governs the apportionment of costly reasoning resources between solution planning and execution.

support.explanation: The source explicitly frames metareasoning around the partition problem between planning and execution.
support.passage: We shall introduce the metareasoning-partitionproblem—the problem of ideally apportioning costly reasoning resources to planning a solution versus applying resource to executing a solution to a problem.
